Override the behaviour of one merged state

mergedState.Rd

Define an exception to the rules inherited by a combination of states. Add the result to mergedStateOverrides in a study configured with mergeStates = TRUE. This definition does not create patient intervals.

Usage

mergedState(members, allowedTransitions, absorbing, label = NULL)

Arguments

members

Character vector containing at least two distinct original state labels. Use exact labels, not merged display labels or state keys. Order does not matter. Labels must not be blank or missing.

allowedTransitions

Optional replacement destinations. A character vector names individual states. A list specifies sets of original members, so list("C", c("C", "D")) permits both C alone and the combination of C and D. character(0) or list() permits no destinations. Omit the argument to inherit transitions. NULL is not accepted.

absorbing

Optional TRUE or FALSE replacing inherited absorbing status. Omit it to inherit. FALSE lets the trajectory continue even when an original member is absorbing.

label

Optional display label. Supply one nonempty, non-missing string. It must not conflict with an original or another explicit display label, even when ignoring case. "0", "START", "EXIT" and "OUT OF COHORT" are reserved, including case variants.

Value

A definition of class c2t_merged_state for the study's mergedStateOverrides list.

Membership and labels

The analyst's original state definitions determine membership. Each source or destination member must refer to an original state. Supply at most one override for each membership set. By default, display labels join the member labels with " + ". Generated label collisions are disambiguated. Labels are never parsed to recover membership, so an original label containing a plus sign remains a single original state.

Inherited rules

Without an explicit destination list, allowed destinations come from the union of the original source members' permissions. Every member newly added at a destination must be permitted by at least one source member. For a self-transition or a transition that only removes members, permission is required for every retained destination member. An empty original allowedStatesList permits all original members.

A combination is absorbing if any member is absorbing, unless absorbing overrides that rule. Absorbing status ends follow-up even when outgoing destinations are listed. An explicit destination list replaces the inherited list without changing absorbing status.

The highest-priority member determines a combination's priority. Larger combinations come first when that priority is equal, followed by state key order. This helper does not override priority.

The resolved membership, label and rules are available in studyEnv$stateDictionary and Data/stateDictionary.rds after generation. Completed study settings retain the original rules and these overrides for a fresh saved-study import.

See also

cohort2TrajectoryConfiguration

Examples

mergedState(c("A", "B"), allowedTransitions = "C", absorbing = FALSE)
mergedState(c("A", "B"), absorbing = FALSE)
mergedState(c("A", "B"), allowedTransitions = list("C", c("C", "D")))
